name: Open Loop Colostomy
overview: Open creation of temporary diverting loop colostomy

pimpingQuestions.question: What are the indications for open loop colostomy in the emergency setting?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Distal large bowel obstruction (sigmoid volvulus after decompression, obstructing cancer), perianal/perineal sepsis (Fournier's gangrene), and fecal diversion for distal anastomotic complications. Open approach is used when laparoscopy is contraindicated (hemodynamic instability, massive distension).

pimpingQuestions.question: What segment of colon is most commonly used for an open loop colostomy?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Transverse colon — it has a true mesentery (mesocolon) providing adequate length to reach the abdominal wall without tension. The sigmoid can also be used but has more variable mesentery length. The site is preoperatively marked by an ET nurse.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the proper technique for opening the bowel in a loop colostomy?
pimpingQuestions.answer: After maturation of the loop on the abdominal wall (usually over a rod/bridge), a transverse incision is made on the anti-mesenteric surface of the proximal (functioning) limb. The incision should be approximately 50-75% of the bowel circumference. Full-thickness incision through all bowel wall layers with mucocutaneous sutures to the skin.

pimpingQuestions.question: What determines proper orientation of the proximal and distal limbs?
pimpingQuestions.answer: The proximal (afferent/functioning) limb should be positioned superiorly in the wound so effluent drains into the stoma appliance. The distal (efferent/defunctioned) limb is inferior. Confirm by tracing the bowel from cecum to anus — incorrect orientation causes appliance management nightmare.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the parastomal hernia rate for loop versus end colostomy?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Loop colostomy: 10-20% (lower than end colostomy because the two bowel limbs partially fill the fascial defect). End colostomy: 30-50%. Both rates are reduced by placing the stoma through the rectus muscle rather than lateral to it.
